findings.evidence: `isHighestWeightVector_iff_forall_e` requires `[IsKilling K L]` (HighestWeight/Basis.lean:32), while `isKilling_typeB` is the sole use of `[LieModule.IsTriangularizable ... (Unit ⊕ Fin (n + 1) ⊕ Fin (n + 1) → K)]` (TypeB/Killing.lean:43 and changed lines 302/314).
findings.fix: Assume `[LieAlgebra.IsKilling K (LieAlgebra.Orthogonal.typeB (Fin (n + 1)) K)]` directly and remove the local `isKilling_typeB` bindings in both declarations. Existing callers with standard-module triangularizability still obtain this instance through `isKilling_typeB`.
findings.issue: The triangularizability hypothesis is stronger than necessary in both this theorem and `nonempty_lieModuleEquiv_typeBSpin_irreducibleQuotient` (Fundamental.lean:54); it is used only to manufacture `IsKilling`.

summary: Both new public theorems unnecessarily require triangularizability of the standard representation instead of the exact Killing-form assumption used by the highest-weight API.
